title: 024 · Why? #12: f(x) = x² from X to Y; range {0, 1, 4} vs codomain and domain (predict-first, white)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Functions. f(x) = x², from X = {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} to Y = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}. What is the range of f? A {0, 1, 4} · B {0, …, 4} · C {−2, …, 2} 👇

A. Square every input: 4, 1, 0, 1, 4. The range is only the outputs actually hit: {0, 1, 4}.
Domain = every input (all of X: that's C). Codomain = every output allowed (all of Y: that's B). The range sits inside the codomain; here 2 and 3 are never hit.
Two inputs on one output (−2 and 2 → 4) is fine. One input with two outputs is not a function.

NDA asked it in 2022 (II), Q13: f(x) = the highest prime factor of x on A = {7, …, 16}, f: A → N. The codomain N never ends, but the range is {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13}: 6 elements.
